thermal-paper-rolls: Use the printer media specification to check width, maximum outside diameter, core and winding. Measure a full replacement roll where possible; a partly used roll cannot establish the original diameter.

direct-thermal-barcode-label-rolls: Supply the printer model, label width and height, core, maximum roll diameter and sensor arrangement. Barcode readability also depends on the printed design, equipment and settings; assess the finished label in the intended workflow.

Describe the surface, application temperature and service conditions for the adhesive. Confirm direct-thermal media requirements rather than assuming that any self-adhesive label will work without a ribbon.
custom-thermal-label-roll: Separate the physical label specification from the artwork. Include label dimensions, printer media requirements, winding and quantity, then explain any preprinted elements or other custom work you want considered.
Custom construction, artwork feasibility, proof steps and minimum quantities need confirmation. Do not approve a roll on appearance alone without checking printer fit and the intended label surface.
thermal-paper-jumbo-rolls: Start with the finished receipt specification and the converting line limits. Include web width, core, diameter, weight and coating orientation, together with the slitting and rewinding requirements.
Agree grade, tolerances, quotation units and handling arrangements. Similar thermal parent-roll listings should be compared using actual technical documents before assuming a material difference.
coloured-jumbo-paper-rolls: Provide the colour reference, intended process and finished product alongside web width, grammage and roll geometry. Where consistency is important, use an agreed physical colour sample rather than a screen image.
Confirm the required grade and whether colour affects the print or converting process. Available shades, batch tolerances and order quantities belong in the quotation.
bopp-packing-tape: Identify carton material, packed weight and whether application uses a hand dispenser or sealing machine. BOPP describes the backing family; it does not by itself specify the adhesive, total thickness or performance.
Request the construction and roll dimensions for the proposed grade. Trial the tape on the actual carton and application process, including the intended service conditions.
custom-packing-tape: Describe the carton-sealing task first, then include any artwork, colour and repeat-layout requirements. Supply quantity and the intended application equipment so the request can be reviewed as a complete packaging specification.
Printing availability, proof approval, minimum order and lead time require confirmation. No particular print process or colour capability is promised by this listing.
bonding-tape: Name both materials and their finishes, and describe the joint geometry and load. Include temperature and indoor or outdoor exposure where relevant. Bonding is a different selection problem from closing a carton.
Discuss adhesive construction, thickness, preparation and trial conditions for the actual materials. The listing does not establish structural strength or a universal service-temperature range.

thermal-paper-roll-size.title: How to Measure a Thermal Paper Roll
thermal-paper-roll-size.description: Measure receipt-roll width, outside diameter and core size, then check the printer requirements before requesting thermal paper.

sections.Start with the printer specification:
A replacement receipt roll needs to fit both the printer mechanism and its paper compartment. Begin with the printer make, model and media specification. An old roll can help you describe what you use, but it may not represent the maximum dimensions the printer supports.

Check the required printing process. A receipt printer that requires thermal media is different from an impact printer using a ribbon. For labels, also check the gap or black-mark sensor and label dimensions. This guide covers the physical measurements of a continuous receipt roll; it does not certify compatibility with a particular printer.
sections.Measure width across the paper:
Width is the distance from one edge of the paper to the other, across the roll. Measure straight across, not diagonally, and record the unit in millimetres. Avoid including protruding core material in the paper-width measurement.

Use the printer manual to determine acceptable width and tolerances. Two rolls with the same nominal width may have different outside diameters or cores. Do not choose a replacement from width alone.
sections.Measure the outside diameter:
The outside diameter is the distance across the full circular face of the roll, through its centre. Measure a new or full roll where possible. A partly used roll will understate the original diameter.

Compare the result with the maximum permitted by the printer. A roll that is too large may prevent the cover from closing or interfere with feeding. Do not force a roll into the compartment. Record whether your measurement describes an existing roll or a maximum equipment limit.
sections.Check the core and mounting arrangement:
Measure the opening through the centre of the core: this is the core inside diameter. If the equipment specification also gives an outside core diameter or spindle requirement, record that separately. Check whether the printer uses a spindle, drop-in loading or another mounting arrangement.

Do not assume that an apparently coreless roll can replace a cored roll, or the reverse. The printer manufacturer's loading instructions take precedence. Include a photograph or the media specification when the mounting arrangement is unclear.
sections.Treat length and paper grade separately:
Roll length describes the amount of paper, not the diameter. The same outside diameter can contain different lengths when paper thickness or core dimensions differ. Ask for the actual quoted length rather than estimating it from a photograph or roll diameter.

Grammage measures mass per area; it is not the same measurement as caliper, which describes thickness. Ask which grade is being quoted and request supporting documentation for chemical composition or image-life requirements. A generic thermal-paper description does not establish those properties.
sections.Confirm loading and storage requirements:
Check the required winding and printable side against the printer instructions. Loading media the wrong way can prevent a usable image even when the physical dimensions fit. Test the proposed grade and settings before placing a substantial production order.

Keep unused rolls in their protective packaging and follow the grade's handling guidance. Heat, sunlight and contact with unsuitable substances can affect thermal media. Where receipts need to remain legible for a defined period, agree the requirement and obtain grade-specific evidence.
sections.Prepare a useful enquiry:
• Printer make and model, with the media specification if available.
  • Paper width and maximum outside diameter in millimetres.
  • Core inside diameter, any outside core limit and loading arrangement.
  • Required roll length, grade and winding information.
  • Number of rolls, preferred packing and intended use.
  • Any documented chemical or image-retention requirements.

Distinguish measured values from requested limits. If a dimension is unknown, identify it as unknown so it can be discussed. Available sizes, packing and quantities are confirmed in the quotation; this checklist is not a list of stocked variants.

thermal-jumbo-roll-specifications.title: Thermal Jumbo Roll Specifications for Converting
thermal-jumbo-roll-specifications.description: Prepare web width, grammage, core, diameter, winding and handling requirements for a thermal parent-roll enquiry.

sections.Define the finished product first:
Thermal jumbo rolls are parent stock for converting equipment. They are not finished rolls intended to fit a point-of-sale printer. Start with the receipt or other finished product you want to produce, its dimensions and its performance requirements.

Provide the converting process and equipment limits. A suitable incoming roll must work with the unwinder, slitter and rewinder as well as the finished product specification. Similar product names are not proof that two grades or formats are interchangeable.
sections.Specify grammage and grade:
Record the required grammage in grams per square metre and identify the grade where known. Include caliper if the converting process or finished-roll design depends on thickness. Grammage alone cannot predict the length that will fit within a given finished-roll diameter.

For thermal material, identify coating and imaging requirements. Ask for documentation for the actual proposed grade if the application requires a chemical declaration, durability claim or other specific property. Do not transfer a claim from a different manufacturer's sheet to an unspecified grade.
sections.Match web width to the slitting plan:
Web width is the width of the incoming sheet of paper wound on the roll. Provide the required width and tolerance, together with the intended finished widths. The converting operator should confirm the slitting layout and any allowance for edge trim.

For example, the total of the finished widths alone does not establish the required parent width if the process also needs trim or other allowances. Agree the layout against the machine and process specification rather than assuming every theoretical combination is practical.
sections.Confirm roll geometry and weight limits:
Record maximum outside diameter, core inside diameter and any core construction requirements. Include maximum permissible roll weight and any restrictions imposed by the chuck, shaft or lifting arrangement.

A roll can meet the width requirement but exceed a weight or diameter limit. Check each constraint independently. Roll length, diameter and mass are related to material properties and core dimensions; obtain the values needed for the order rather than substituting one for another.
sections.Describe winding and coating orientation:
State how the roll must unwind and which side must face the relevant part of the process. Use a drawing or a clear orientation reference when words such as inside, outside, left and right could be misunderstood.

Include any requirements for winding tension, splice handling, edge quality and tolerances from the machine or quality specification. These must be agreed with the proposed supply; a general catalogue listing does not guarantee a particular converting limit.
sections.Plan receiving, handling and approval:
Confirm that the receiving site can unload and handle the proposed roll dimensions and mass using suitable equipment and trained personnel. Agree protective packing, storage guidance and the information needed on roll labels. This guide does not replace the equipment manufacturer's safety instructions or your site procedures.

Where process performance is critical, ask what samples or trial arrangements can be provided. Agree how the grade and trial results will be approved before a larger order. Availability of samples, documents or a specific grade must be confirmed.
sections.Agree quotation units and required infor:
• Finished product and converting process.
  • Grade, grammage, caliper and relevant documentation.
  • Web width, tolerances and slitting layout.
  • Core requirements, outside diameter and maximum roll weight.
  • Winding direction and coating orientation.
  • Order quantity, packing and receiving constraints.
  • Quotation unit, such as mass or rolls, and what the stated quantity includes.

Keep required limits separate from measured examples. Include machine documentation where possible and identify unknown values. A quotation should resolve the actual available specification, minimum quantities and delivery arrangements before an order is agreed.

The registered identity of the organisation responsible for processing your information must be confirmed before this draft is finalised. Our Legal Notice contains the available business contact information.

browsing.title: Browsing and hosting
browsing.body:
Our website and mailbox use Hostinger services. When you visit, the hosting infrastructure processes connection information needed to deliver pages, such as your IP address, request time, requested URL and browser information. Server and security logs may record this information to operate the service and investigate faults or abuse.

The purpose is to provide a reliable, secure website. Our legitimate interest in operating and protecting the service is the basis for this processing under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. The hosting account's log retention settings require confirmation.

enquiries.title: Contact and product enquiries
enquiries.body:
The enquiry form collects your name, email address and message, together with the selected product when applicable. We send these details to our business mailbox to review your request and reply. Your email address is used as the reply address. Please include only information relevant to your enquiry.

These fields are required to submit the form, but contacting us is voluntary. You may instead email us directly. Without suitable contact details, we may be unable to respond.

For steps you request before entering a contract with us, processing is based on Article 6(1)(b) GDPR. For general questions or correspondence with someone acting for a business, it is based on our legitimate interest in responding to business enquiries under Article 6(1)(f). Sending an enquiry does not subscribe you to marketing.

cookies.title: Cookies and form security
cookies.body:
The website sets a first-party session cookie named kraus_session. It links your browser to security tokens, submission status and, when needed, temporarily retained form values. This protects the enquiry form and helps prevent duplicate messages. It is a session cookie without a fixed expiry date; browsers normally remove it when the session ends, although session restoration can preserve it.

The application also uses a hidden spam-trap field and limits repeated submissions. Its rate-limit record contains a hashed IP address, a request count and an expiry time, not your message. A hash is still treated as personal data, rather than anonymous information.

These measures support our legitimate interest in preventing abuse under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. Necessary session storage supports the form service you request. Blocking cookies may prevent the form from working; direct email remains available.

The current website code does not include advertising cookies, analytics trackers, third-party CAPTCHA, embedded maps or remotely loaded fonts. We will review this notice and any required consent controls before introducing optional tracking.

recipients.title: Who receives information
recipients.body:
Enquiries are available to the people handling business correspondence and to the hosting and email providers needed to operate those services. Hostinger processes website and mailbox data as part of providing those services. Information may also be disclosed where necessary to meet a legal obligation or establish, exercise or defend a legal claim.

The applicable Hostinger contracting entity, processing locations, subprocessors and any safeguards for transfers outside the European Economic Area must be verified against our service agreement before publication. We do not claim that all data stays in Germany or the EEA. Provider information is available in Hostinger's privacy policy; that policy does not replace this notice.

retention.title: How long information is kept
retention.body:
Enquiry correspondence should be kept only while needed to answer the request, manage the resulting business relationship or meet applicable recordkeeping and legal-claim requirements. The mailbox deletion schedule and backup retention must be confirmed before this draft is published.

Form values may temporarily remain in the server session after a failed submission without JavaScript. Session data is removed according to the server's session cleanup settings. The form does not maintain a separate database of enquiry messages.

Rate-limit entries apply to a 15-minute window. Expired entries are removed when a subsequent submission successfully rewrites the rate-limit file; they are not guaranteed to be physically deleted at exactly 15 minutes. Hosting logs and email copies have separate retention settings.

rights.title: Your privacy rights
rights.body:
Subject to the applicable conditions, you can request access, correction, erasure, restriction and portability of your personal data. You may object to processing based on legitimate interests for reasons relating to your situation. Where processing relies on consent, you may withdraw it for future processing.

Use the contact details above to exercise your rights. You can also complain to a data protection authority, including the authority where you live or work. For North Rhine-Westphalia, see the LDI NRW complaints page.

The enquiry form does not make automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, or create marketing profiles. Its automated security checks can reject or temporarily limit submissions; you can contact us by email instead.

enquiry.title: Submitting an enquiry
enquiry.body:
Provide accurate contact information and enough detail for us to understand your request. An enquiry asks us for information or a quotation; it does not place an order or create a purchase obligation.

The form's delivery confirmation means that the email service accepted the message. It is not an order confirmation, a quotation or a promise of a response within a particular time. If you do not receive a reply, contact info@krauspapersgmbh.com.

orders.title: Quotations and orders
orders.body:
Before an order is concluded, the parties must agree the relevant product specification, price, taxes, payment arrangements, delivery terms and any applicable sales conditions. Returns, complaints and other contractual matters are governed by the applicable agreement and mandatory law.

Nothing on this page removes statutory rights or introduces unconfirmed payment, cancellation, warranty or jurisdiction terms.

use.title: Responsible use
use.body:
Use this website lawfully. Do not submit spam, impersonate another person, attempt unauthorised access or interfere with the service. Automated security measures may limit repeated form submissions.

Website text, design and images may be protected by intellectual property rights. Third-party product names and trademarks remain the property of their respective owners. Uses beyond those permitted by law require permission from the relevant rights holder.

availability.title: Availability and external links
availability.body:
Pages may change or be temporarily unavailable during maintenance or technical incidents. Please tell us if you find an error so that we can review it.

Links to external websites are provided for further information. Those websites are operated by their respective providers and have their own terms and privacy notices. These terms do not exclude liability where exclusion is prohibited by law.
